Original CT information courtesy of Dr. Tobias Schwarz

scans.attribution_text: "Domestic Cat (Felis catus)" by The University of Edinburgh Open.Ed (original CT information courtesy of Dr Tobias Schwarz; adapted and prepared by Brian Mather, The Royal (Dick) School of Veterinary Studies, The University of Edinburgh), https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/domestic-cat-felis-catus-7c99ca836d834c39872ecf5e9b5e2087, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
scans.changes: Rounds 1-4 used it as the skull under the CatBaseV6 art study: aligned to the midsagittal plane, scaled 2.2x, pitched 12 deg, Laplacian-smoothed, converted to a level set and used only as the bone surface under a procedurally sculpted soft-tissue skin. Round 5 (2026-09-26) keeps it for landmarks only: its orbits place the eye globes, and a tissue-depth fit checks the scan-derived head against it; no CT surface is part of the round-5 skin. Round 6 (2026-09-26) keeps the same role; the globes sit 2 mm further forward along the gaze than the orbit placement. Round 7 (2026-09-26) keeps the same landmark-only role and eye placement. Round 8 (2026-09-26) keeps the landmark-only role; the globes sit a further 2.5 mm forward, and the round-5 finding that the CT vertex stands ~14 mm above the scanned crown sets the round-8 crown lift. No CT triangles are stored in the .blend or shipped. The raw scan stays private (Local/ThirdPartyRaw).

scans.name: Cat sitting upright
scans.role: elaughli Cat sitting upright scan: geometric ground truth of the round-5 head and neck
scans.license_requirements: Author must be credited. Commercial use is allowed.
scans.description_excerpt: This is the most successful scan of her while she’s awake. I still couldn’t quite make it all the way around before she moved though.
scans.acquisition_note: copied from earlier evaluation file /tmp/sora-cat-scan-eval/elaughli-cat-sitting-upright.glb (originally from the Objaverse mirror)

mirror_license.note: The collection is ODC-By 1.0; each object keeps its own Sketchfab license (re-read per object).

scans.attribution_text: "Cat sitting upright" by elaughli, https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/cat-sitting-upright-3ffbfcabc4c34b58b03d43fd4f445b54, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)
scans.changes: Adapted in round 5 (2026-09-26) as the geometric ground truth of the CatBaseV6 head and neck (scripts/art/create_cat_base_v7.py). Taken: the shape of the scanned surface of the head, face, cheeks, throat, nape and upper neck, from the clean left half only; nothing else (no vertex colour, texture, topology or ears). Changed: expressed in a head frame found by mirror-ICP (the head was turned about 85 deg on the body); the noisy right half discarded and replaced by the mirror image of the left; converted to a 0.5 mm signed distance field with tunnels under 8 mm (the open ear canals) sealed and smoothed 0.7-2.2 mm to remove fur-clump noise; the laid-back noisy pinnae removed by a morphological opening and replaced by new modelled pinnae; inset 1-15 mm by region (the thickness of the new groom) to turn the fur surface into a skin; scaled 1.874x and pitched 5 deg onto the round-4 face profile (the scan is not metric); faded out below the neck into an original biped bust; new eyes, lids, nose leather, lip and whisker-pad details, markings and groom. Round 6 (2026-09-26, scripts/art/create_cat_base_v8.py) keeps the same scan field and changes only what is layered on it: throat and neck insets reduced to 4.5 and 11 mm, a smooth conchal bowl and funnel carved under each new pinna instead of the round-5 cup, and a narrower, higher original bust. Round 7 (2026-09-26, scripts/art/create_cat_base_v9.py) samples the same scan field through a smooth warp in front of the eyes (the muzzle and nose 11 mm forward, the lower muzzle, lips and chin 8 mm up, so the upper lip is shorter), fills the hollows left round the removed scan ears with a morphological closing (r 6 scan units) and two capsule plugs in the open canal pits, insets the neck sides up to 15 mm more and the nape 15 mm, replaces the round-6 bowl carve by a concha voxelised from each new pinna, and adds new surface details (a domed nose pad, a nasal bridge and stop, a chin, puffier whisker pads, a lid fill band round each eye) and a new original bust with scapulae and forelimbs. Round 8 (2026-09-26, scripts/art/create_cat_base_v10.py) keeps the same scan field and changes how it is sampled and what is layered on it: floating remnants of the scanned pinnae dropped, then a morphological opening (r 7 scan units), a wider closing (r 14) and a heavy blur round the former ears and the scanned canals, so the scan's old ear canals, sockets and ear ledge are gone (the round-7 canal plugs removed); the cranium behind the ears 18 % shorter and the occiput 10 % flatter (a smooth warp), the crown lifted up to 13 mm, the temples pared up to 3 mm, the muzzle warp cut from 11 to 9 mm and the chin raised 10 mm and tucked 4 mm back; neck side and nape insets cut to 2 and 9 mm; new modelled pinnae whose back and margins flare into the head skin, a concha carved only in front of each inner face with a canal tube, and new surface details (a flat nose planum, a deeper stop, a mentum crease) and a new original bust. The committed .blend stores a new QuadriFlow quad cage and the decimated derived level set it is shrink-wrapped onto (the sculpt target); no scan triangle, vertex colour or texture is stored or shipped. The raw scan stays private (Local/ThirdPartyRaw).
